newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts sag with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts sag with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging market debts moved lower in sympathy with U.S. Treasuries and equities, traders said.
"People look at U.S. assets and wonder if the January rally is over," said a trader with a major U.S. bank.
Spreads have widened, but many market watchers remained upbeat about the market's longer term performance.
It was generally agreed that the emerging market debts going forward could not keep up with its neck-breaking pace of gains since beginning of the year, but a sudden shift downward appeared unlikely.
"Nothing fundamental has changed," said James Barrineau, emerging market fixed income specialist at Smith Barney. "The economic outlook remains favorable."
In a volatile market environment, traders tended to become more sensitive to signs of social unrest which would have been downplayed in a rising market, he said.
The case in point is the labor protests in Venezuela and gathering discontent in Ecuador, Barrineau said.
Venezuela PARs fell 1-1/8 to 67-1/8 bid and Venesuela DCBs lost 5/8 to 90-3/8 bid.
Ecuador PDI was off 5/8 at 65-1/8 bid.
Traders noted that sentiment on Mexico had turned mildly bearish since the release of the inflation data late Thursday.
Mexican consumer prices rose 1.60 percent for Janaury 1-15, at the high end of the estimates. Both Mexican equities and money market instruments reacted negatively to the data, they said.

Steadily declining trader surplus was also worrying, they added. The government reported the surplus in December was $220 million, down from $254 million in Novemer and October. In September the surplus stood as high as $684 million.
Mexico Pars fell 3/4 to 90-1/4 bid and UMS-26 lost 7/8 to 108-1/4.
Russia should have received a boost from the passage of its budget in the Duma, but prices were weighed down by the falling prices of other emerging debts, traders said.
Russia dollar Vnesh dropped 1 point to 79-1/4, but Minfins held much better, with Min Fin 5 eased merely 1/8 to bid 41-3/4.

The deadlock between Bulgaria's ruling socialists and the opposition over the formation of a new government put pressure on the already fragile Bulgaria Bradies and the prices slid further in choppy U.S. trading, traders said.
